about: What each tool checks, over which files, and how far from clean each one is
allowed to be. A ceiling, not evidence: nothing here is produced by a run,
CI never signs it, and moving a number is a deliberate visible diff.
Read bin/quality-contract.py for the mechanism. Two rules make this a
ratchet rather than an excuse list, and both are enforced:
Totality. Every tracked first-party *.py lands in exactly one cell per
tool. A file in no cell is one nobody decided about; a file in two is a
decision that contradicts itself.
Ceilings are checked, not prose. A cell fails when its measurement
exceeds its ceiling. The previous declaration carried counts in comment
text, which stayed green at any number: it was enforced in one direction
only, so an entry matching nothing failed while '241 findings' passed at
Reasons say what, never how many. A reason names the kind of work a cell
holds and why it has the tier it has; the counting belongs to the ceiling
beside it, which is the half that gets compared. Reasons went false in
exactly the way the old comment text did -- four of them, two naming a
cell that had been deleted outright -- because fixing that property for
the ceiling had left the prose next to it unchecked. verify now rejects a
bare numeral in a reason. Rule names keep their digits: NPY002 names a
kind of finding and stays true however many there are.
A ceiling only ever falls. Raising one is how a backlog grows while it is
supposedly being worked, so it is a change that has to be argued for in a
pull request rather than absorbed by re-running --update-baseline.
